title: The pullback on etale cohomology is well defined and functorial
statement:
For a morphism of schemes $u:Y\to X$ [def-pc-scheme] and an abelian sheaf $G$ on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], let $u^*:H^q(X_{\Et},G)\to H^q(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}G)$ be the pullback map of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], built from a K-injective resolution $s:G\to I^\bullet$ and a K-injective resolution $r:u^{-1}I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], as $\mathcal H^q$ of $a\mapsto r(\eta_u(a))$, $\eta_u$ the unit of $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For a morphism $\varphi:G\to G'$ of abelian sheaves on a scheme $T$ and K-injective resolutions $G\to I^\bullet$, $G'\to I'^\bullet$, write $H^q(\varphi):H^q(T_{\Et},G)\to H^q(T_{\Et},G')$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] for $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(T,\tilde\varphi))$, where $\tilde\varphi:I^\bullet\to I'^\bullet$ is any morphism of complexes with $\tilde\varphi\circ(G\to I^\bullet)$ homotopic to $(G'\to I'^\bullet)\circ\varphi$; such $\tilde\varphi$ exist and $H^q(\varphi)$ does not depend on $\tilde\varphi$ (step 1), and for $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_G$ these are the identifications of the groups computed from different resolutions [prop-weil-pbc-cohomology-resolution-independent]. Then:

1. (Independence.) $u^*$ does not depend on the choice of $I^\bullet$ and $J^\bullet$: for a second choice $(I'^\bullet,J'^\bullet)$ the two maps $u^*$ agree after the identifications $H^q(\mathrm{id}_G)$ and $H^q(\mathrm{id}_{u^{-1}G})$. The same holds for $u^*:\RGamma(X_{\Et},K)\to\RGamma(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}K)$, $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], as a morphism of $\Dplus(\Ab)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] up to the canonical isomorphisms between the complexes computed from different resolutions.
2. (Any comparison complex.) Let $t:u^{-1}G\to M^\bullet$ be a quasi-isomorphism to a bounded below complex of abelian sheaves on $Y_{\Et}$ and $\beta:u^{-1}I^\bullet\to M^\bullet$ a morphism of complexes with $\beta\circ u^{-1}(s)=t$. Let $\gamma:M^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ be a morphism of complexes with $\gamma\circ t$ homotopic to $r\circ u^{-1}(s)$ (it exists, unique up to homotopy). Then $u^*=\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(Y,\gamma))\circ\mathcal H^q\bigl(a\mapsto\beta(\eta_u(a))\bigr)$, the second map being $\mathcal H^q$ of $\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(Y,M^\bullet)$. If $M^\bullet$ is K-injective, or a complex of $\Gamma(Y,-)$-acyclic sheaves, then $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(Y,\gamma))$ is an isomorphism, so that $u^*$ is computed on $\Gamma(Y,M^\bullet)$ by $a\mapsto\beta(\eta_u(a))$.
3. (Naturality.) For a morphism $\varphi:G\to G'$ of abelian sheaves on $X_{\Et}$, $u^*\circ H^q(\varphi)=H^q(u^{-1}\varphi)\circ u^*$.
4. (Composition.) For a morphism $v:Z\to Y$, let $c_{u,v}:v^{-1}u^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(u\circ v)^{-1}$ be the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (compatible with the units). Then $(u\circ v)^*=H^q(c_{u,v,G})\circ v^*\circ u^*:H^q(X_{\Et},G)\to H^q(Z_{\Et},(u\circ v)^{-1}G)$, and, with $e_X:\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ of the same lemma, $H^q(e_{X,G})\circ\mathrm{id}_X^*=\mathrm{id}$.
5. (Etale maps.) If $u$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], let $\rho_G:u^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}G|_Y$ be the identification of the inverse image with the restriction, $G|_Y(V)=G(V)$ for $V$ etale over $Y$, of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]. If $G\to I^\bullet$ is a resolution by a bounded below complex of injective abelian sheaves, then $u^{-1}G\to u^{-1}I^\bullet$ is a resolution of $u^{-1}G$ by a bounded below complex of injective abelian sheaves, one may take $J^\bullet=u^{-1}I^\bullet$, $r=\mathrm{id}$, and then $u^*$ is $\mathcal H^q$ of the restriction map $\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)=I^\bullet(X)\to I^\bullet(Y)\cong\Gamma(Y,u^{-1}I^\bullet)$ (through $\rho_{I^\bullet}(Y)$) along $u:Y\to X$.

proof.text: *Lifting principle (and its consequences).* Let $\mathcal A=\Ab(T_{\Et})$ for a scheme $T$, let $\sigma:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ be a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of $\mathcal A$ and $I^\bullet$ a K-injective complex. Then $-\circ\sigma:\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(B^\bullet,I^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(A^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ is bijective. Indeed, by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] the localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] induces bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(N^\bullet,I^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(QN^\bullet,QI^\bullet)$ for $N^\bullet=A^\bullet,B^\bullet$; since $Q$ is a functor, $Q(g\circ\sigma)=Q(g)\circ Q(\sigma)$, so these bijections carry $-\circ\sigma$ to $-\circ Q(\sigma)$, which is bijective because $Q(\sigma)$ is an isomorphism of $D(\mathcal A)$ ($Q$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms). Consequences used below. (a) For K-injective resolutions $s:G\to I^\bullet$, $s':G'\to I'^\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] and $\varphi:G\to G'$, applying this to $\sigma=s$ and the class of $s'\circ\varphi$ gives $\tilde\varphi:I^\bullet\to I'^\bullet$ with $\tilde\varphi s\simeq s'\varphi$, unique up to homotopy; the same holds for complexes $K^\bullet$ in place of $G$. (b) An additive functor, here $\Gamma(T,-)$, carries a homotopy $h$ between morphisms of complexes to the homotopy $\Gamma(T,h)$, so homotopic morphisms induce the same maps $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(T,-))$; hence $H^q(\varphi)$ of the statement is well defined, and $H^q(\varphi'\circ\varphi)=H^q(\varphi')\circ H^q(\varphi)$, $H^q(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$ (a composite of lifts is a lift of the composite, the identity a lift of the identity); for $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_G$ the lifts are the mutually inverse homotopy equivalences of [prop-weil-pbc-cohomology-resolution-independent]. (c) (Two out of three.) If $\gamma\circ\sigma\simeq\tau$ with $\sigma,\tau$ quasi-isomorphisms, then $\mathcal H^q(\gamma)\mathcal H^q(\sigma)=\mathcal H^q(\tau)$ (homotopic maps agree on cohomology), so $\mathcal H^q(\gamma)=\mathcal H^q(\tau)\mathcal H^q(\sigma)^{-1}$ is bijective and $\gamma$ is a quasi-isomorphism. (d) $u^{-1}$ is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], hence commutes with the cohomology of complexes [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] and carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms; a composite of quasi-isomorphisms is one.

source.place: Lemma Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), (1) implies (2); for bounded below complexes of injectives Lemmas Tag 013P (lemma-morphisms-lift) and Tag 013S (lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy)

proof.text: *Clause 3 (naturality).* Let $s:G\to I^\bullet$, $r:u^{-1}I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ and $s':G'\to I'^\bullet$, $r':u^{-1}I'^\bullet\to J'^\bullet$ be the resolutions defining $u^*$ for $G$ and $G'$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. By step 1(a) choose $\tilde\varphi:I^\bullet\to I'^\bullet$ with $\tilde\varphi s\simeq s'\varphi$; it computes $H^q(\varphi)$. The complex $J'^\bullet$ is K-injective and $r\circ u^{-1}(s):u^{-1}G\to J^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism (step 1(d)), and $r:u^{-1}I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ is one, so step 1 gives $\psi:J^\bullet\to J'^\bullet$ with $\psi r\simeq r'\circ u^{-1}(\tilde\varphi)$. Then $\psi\circ(r\,u^{-1}(s))\simeq r'u^{-1}(\tilde\varphi s)\simeq r'u^{-1}(s')\circ u^{-1}(\varphi)$ ($u^{-1}$ is additive, so it preserves homotopies), so $\psi$ is a lift of $u^{-1}\varphi$ and computes $H^q(u^{-1}\varphi)$. Naturality of the unit [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] gives $\eta_{u,I'^\bullet}\circ\tilde\varphi=u_*u^{-1}(\tilde\varphi)\circ\eta_{u,I^\bullet}$ exactly; on global sections, with $\Gamma(X,u_*-)=\Gamma(Y,-)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], this says $\eta_u(\tilde\varphi(a))=u^{-1}(\tilde\varphi)(\eta_u(a))$. Hence the two morphisms of complexes $\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(Y,J'^\bullet)$, $a\mapsto r'(\eta_u(\tilde\varphi(a)))=r'u^{-1}(\tilde\varphi)(\eta_u(a))$ and $a\mapsto\psi(r(\eta_u(a)))$, are homotopic ($\Gamma(Y,-)$ of the homotopy $\psi r\simeq r'u^{-1}(\tilde\varphi)$), so they agree on $\mathcal H^q$ (step 1(b)): $u^*\circ H^q(\varphi)=H^q(u^{-1}\varphi)\circ u^*$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 01F8 (lemma-functoriality: the construction is functorial in the triple) and Remark Tag 01FB (remark-explain-arrow: the map $\beta$ chosen by Derived Categories, Lemma 013P); written there for ringed spaces, the etale case being the same argument with the etale $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$

proof.text: *Clause 1 (independence).* Apply step 2 with $G'=G$, $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_G$, the first choice $(I^\bullet,J^\bullet)$ for $G$ and the second $(I'^\bullet,J'^\bullet)$ for $G'$: $u^*{}'\circ H^q(\mathrm{id}_G)=H^q(\mathrm{id}_{u^{-1}G})\circ u^*$, and $H^q(\mathrm{id})$ are the identifications of [prop-weil-pbc-cohomology-resolution-independent] (step 1(b)). For $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ represented by a bounded below complex $K^\bullet$ the same argument applies verbatim with $K^\bullet$ in place of $G$ and $u^{-1}K^\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] in place of $u^{-1}G$ (step 1 is stated for complexes): the two morphisms of complexes $\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(Y,J'^\bullet)$ obtained are homotopic, so they have the same class in $K(\Ab)$ and hence in $\Dplus(\Ab)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], where $\Gamma(X,\tilde\varphi)$ and $\Gamma(Y,\psi)$ are the canonical isomorphisms between the complexes $\RGamma$ computed from the two choices (homotopy equivalences, step 1(a)).

source.place: Section Tag 01F7, the paragraph defining equation Tag 01F9 (equation-functorial-derived) and Remark Tag 01FB

proof.text: *Clause 2 (any comparison complex).* Since $J^\bullet$ is K-injective and $t$ is a quasi-isomorphism, step 1 gives $\gamma:M^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ with $\gamma t\simeq r\,u^{-1}(s)$, unique up to homotopy. The morphisms $\gamma\beta$ and $r$ from $u^{-1}I^\bullet$ to the K-injective $J^\bullet$ satisfy $\gamma\beta\circ u^{-1}(s)=\gamma t\simeq r\circ u^{-1}(s)$, and $u^{-1}(s)$ is a quasi-isomorphism (step 1(d)); by the injectivity in step 1, $\gamma\beta\simeq r$. Applying $\Gamma(Y,-)$ (step 1(b)), $a\mapsto r(\eta_u(a))$ and $a\mapsto\gamma(\beta(\eta_u(a)))$ agree on $\mathcal H^q$, i.e. $u^*=\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(Y,\gamma))\circ\mathcal H^q(a\mapsto\beta(\eta_u(a)))$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. By step 1(c), $\gamma$ is a quasi-isomorphism ($t$ and $r\,u^{-1}(s)$ are). If $M^\bullet$ is K-injective, a quasi-isomorphism between K-injective complexes is a homotopy equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] (last sentence), so $\Gamma(Y,\gamma)$ is a homotopy equivalence and $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(Y,\gamma))$ is bijective.

source.place: Remark Tag 01FB (remark-explain-arrow): the map $\beta$ into a resolution $(\mathcal J')^\bullet$ and the vertical quasi-isomorphism inverted in the derived category

proof.text: *Clause 2, acyclic case.* Let $M^\bullet$ be bounded below with $\Gamma(Y,-)$-acyclic terms. Choose a resolution $M^\bullet\to L^\bullet$ by a bounded below complex of injectives; it is K-injective [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and $u^{-1}G\to M^\bullet\to L^\bullet$ is a K-injective resolution of $u^{-1}G$. By the acyclicity criterion for complexes [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] (3), applied to the left exact additive functor $v=\Gamma(Y,-)$ on the Grothendieck abelian category $\Ab(Y_{\Et})$, $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(Y,M^\bullet))\to\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(Y,L^\bullet))$ is bijective. The lift $\gamma':L^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ of $\mathrm{id}_{u^{-1}G}$ (step 1(a)) is a quasi-isomorphism between K-injective complexes (step 1(c)), hence a homotopy equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], and by uniqueness in step 1 $\gamma\simeq\gamma'\circ(M^\bullet\to L^\bullet)$ (both are lifts of $r\,u^{-1}(s)$ along $t$). So $\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(Y,\gamma))$ is a composite of two bijections.

source.place: Proposition Tag 05TA (proposition-enough-acyclics), (1): a bounded below complex whose terms are acyclic computes RF, and Lemma Tag 015E (lemma-leray-acyclicity); used in literature/stacks-project/cohomology.tex Remark Tag 01FB through Lemma Tag 01EZ (lemma-before-Leray)

proof.text: *Clause 4 (composition).* Choose $s:G\to I^\bullet$ and $r:u^{-1}I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ defining $u^*$, and $r':v^{-1}J^\bullet\to L^\bullet$ a K-injective resolution on $Z_{\Et}$, so that $v^*$ for $u^{-1}G$ is computed from $r\,u^{-1}(s)$ and $r'$ by $b\mapsto r'(\eta_v(b))$. Hence $v^*u^*$ is $\mathcal H^q$ of $a\mapsto r'(\eta_{v,J}(r(\eta_{u,I}(a))))$. Naturality of $\eta_v$ gives $\eta_{v,J}\circ r=v_*v^{-1}(r)\circ\eta_{v,u^{-1}I}$, so this is $a\mapsto r''\bigl(u_*(\eta_{v,u^{-1}I})(\eta_{u,I}(a))\bigr)$ with $r''=r'\circ v^{-1}(r):v^{-1}u^{-1}I^\bullet\to L^\bullet$, a quasi-isomorphism (step 1(d)) to a K-injective complex. By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2), $u_*v_*(c_{u,v,I})\circ u_*(\eta_{v,u^{-1}I})\circ\eta_{u,I}=d_{u,v}\circ\eta_{u\circ v,I}$; on global sections $d_{u,v}$ is the identification $\Gamma(X,(u\circ v)_*F)=F(Z)=\Gamma(X,u_*v_*F)$, so $u_*(\eta_{v,u^{-1}I})(\eta_{u,I}(a))=c_{u,v,I}^{-1}(\eta_{u\circ v,I}(a))$. Therefore $v^*u^*$ is the map $(u\circ v)^*$ computed (clause 1) with the K-injective resolution $r''\circ c_{u,v,I}^{-1}:(u\circ v)^{-1}I^\bullet\to L^\bullet$ of $(u\circ v)^{-1}G$, followed by the identification of the target $H^q(Z,v^{-1}u^{-1}G)$, computed from $r''\circ v^{-1}u^{-1}(s)$, with $H^q(Z,(u\circ v)^{-1}G)$, computed from $r''c_{u,v,I}^{-1}(u\circ v)^{-1}(s)$. By naturality of $c_{u,v}$, $r''c_{u,v,I}^{-1}(u\circ v)^{-1}(s)\circ c_{u,v,G}=r''\circ v^{-1}u^{-1}(s)$, so $\mathrm{id}_{L^\bullet}$ is a lift of $c_{u,v,G}$ and that identification is $H^q(c_{u,v,G})$ (step 1(b)): $(u\circ v)^*=H^q(c_{u,v,G})\circ v^*\circ u^*$. For the identity: by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (3), $e_{X,I}\circ d_X\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id},I}=\mathrm{id}$, so with $J^\bullet=I^\bullet$ and $r=e_{X,I}:\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}I^\bullet\to I^\bullet$, $\mathrm{id}_X^*$ is $\mathcal H^q$ of $a\mapsto e_{X,I}(\eta_{\mathrm{id},I}(a))=a$, from $H^q(X,G)$ computed by $s$ to $H^q(X,\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}G)$ computed by $e_{X,I}\circ\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}(s)=s\circ e_{X,G}$; so $\mathrm{id}_{I^\bullet}$ lifts $e_{X,G}$ and $H^q(e_{X,G})\circ\mathrm{id}_X^*=\mathrm{id}$.

proof.text: *Clause 5 (etale maps).* Let $u$ be etale and $s:G\to I^\bullet$ a resolution by a bounded below complex of injective abelian sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] (applied with the constant ring $\mathbf Z$, abelian sheaves being $\mathbf Z$-module sheaves), $u^{-1}$ has the exact left adjoint $u_!$ and therefore carries injective sheaves to injective sheaves; and $u^{-1}$ is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], so $u^{-1}(s):u^{-1}G\to u^{-1}I^\bullet$ is a resolution by a bounded below complex of injectives, hence a K-injective resolution [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. So $J^\bullet=u^{-1}I^\bullet$, $r=\mathrm{id}$ is an admissible choice in [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] (any other choice gives the same $u^*$ by clause 1), and $u^*$ is $\mathcal H^q$ of $a\mapsto\eta_{u,I}(a)\in\Gamma(Y,u^{-1}I^\bullet)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (2), $\rho_{I}(Y)\circ\eta_{u,I}(X):I^\bullet(X)\to I^\bullet(Y)$ is the restriction along $u$, and $\rho_I(Y):\Gamma(Y,u^{-1}I^\bullet)\to I^\bullet(Y)$ is an isomorphism of complexes (naturality of $\rho$ in the sheaf). Hence $u^*$ is $\mathcal H^q$ of the restriction $\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)\to I^\bullet(Y)$, as claimed.

split_report.summary: Split into seven steps following Stacks cohomology.tex 01F7-01FB, derived.tex 070I and sites-cohomology.tex 03F3. Step 1 derives the lifting principle for K-injective targets (Stacks 070I (1)=>(2)) from the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived, with its consequences (comparison maps unique up to homotopy, homotopies survive Gamma, two-out-of-three, u^{-1} preserves quasi-isomorphisms). Naturality (3) is proved first from naturality of the unit; independence (1) is its case phi = id, also for RGamma. Clause (2) was corrected: the old text composed u^* with a 'canonical map H^q(Y,u^{-1}G) -> H^q(Gamma(Y,M))' that does not exist for an arbitrary comparison complex M; the map goes the other way, via gamma: M -> J, and is bijective when M is K-injective or Gamma-acyclic (lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity (3)). H^q(phi) is now defined in the statement. Composition (4) uses the new node lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition (c_{u,v} compatible with the units, d_{u,v}: (uv)_* = u_*v_* up to the fibre-product isomorphism; e_X for the identity, whose identity clause was stated as id^* = id although the targets differ by e_X). Etale case (5) uses lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives (exact left adjoint u_!) and the new node lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction (u^{-1}G = G|_Y, unit = restriction). New nodes searched three ways; neither in Mathlib.
